edition_or_version: As discussed in Koopman and Widen (arXiv 2404.16768)
requirement_paraphrase: Per the authors: UL 4600 defines safe as acceptable post-mitigation item-level risk as defined by the safety case; they cite summing total item risk (prompt element 6.1.1.3.a) as a recommended approach; UL 4600 uses SPIs and field engineering feedback for continuous improvement.

instrument: Koopman and Widen, redefining safety for autonomous vehicles
requirement_paraphrase: Argues current safety definitions assume human supervision and need revision for driverless operation (open world, self-enforced limits, ad hoc system of systems, legal/ethical constraints); contrasts ISO 26262, ISO 21448, UL 4600, DefStan 00-56.

instrument: Defeaters and Eliminative Argumentation in Assurance 2.0
requirement_paraphrase: Argues that assurance cases should record defeaters (doubts) and investigate them; a case is closed only with no unsupported claims and no active defeaters.

status_note: Secondary description of the published standard
clause_or_section_seen: Clause 6.5 (acceptance criterion), clause 10 (known hazardous scenarios), clause 11 (unknown scenarios), Annex C.2.2, C.3 (as cited by authors)
requirement_paraphrase: Per the paper: the standard has the developer derive an acceptance criterion for residual risk, then show validation targets are met across known-hazardous and unknown scenario sets; lists risk acceptance rationales (ALARP, MEM, PRB, GAME/GAMAB).

instrument: Toward an Agricultural Operational Design Domain: A Framework (arXiv 2511.02937)
clause_or_section_seen: Sections 4.2 and Tables 1-2 (as described by fetch)
requirement_paraphrase: Says existing ODD concepts do not comprehensively fit agricultural/off-road machinery; proposes ODD attributes including dust (e.g. a no-dust visibility condition) and lists GNSS in a digital-information layer.

status_note: Listed as current; part of an ASAM pilot for a new process
requirement_paraphrase: Provides a UML data model and exchange formats (e.g. YAML, OpenSCENARIO DSL) for describing operational, current and target operational domains of ADS.

Secondary summary: 2025 edition adds operating-mode requirements (lockable selector), robot Classes I and II, cybersecurity requirements to the extent they affect safety, and absorbs collaborative requirements formerly in ISO/TS 15066.

status_note: In force; Annex III section 3 text still not retrieved from official source (2026-10-12 attempt); item numbers 3.1.1, 3.2.4, 3.3.x, 3.6.3.3 remain unverified
requirement_paraphrase: New definitions (autonomous mobile machinery, supervisor, supervisory function); control system must perform the safety functions by itself even with remote supervisory function; movement must account for risks related to the intended operating area; additions on travelling function and control-circuit failure; new section 3.6.3.3 on autonomous mobile machinery (content not given in source).

instrument: SAE J3016 Taxonomy and Definitions for Driving Automation
requirement_paraphrase: Defines ODD as operating conditions under which a driving automation system is designed to function, including environmental, geographical and time-of-day restrictions and/or required traffic or roadway characteristics; per Note 1, rapid transient changes (e.g. inclement weather) do not necessarily represent an ODD exit.

instrument: Dubai Executive Council Resolution No. (3) of 2019 (testing autonomous vehicles)
requirement_paraphrase: Testing requires an RTA contract and Authorisation; RTA sets safety standards for each test phase and designates roads and times; establishments file periodic stage reports and carry insurance.

instrument: Dubai Law No. (9) of 2023 Regulating the Operation of Autonomous Vehicles
edition_or_version: Issued 6 Apr 2023; effect 90 days after publication (Art. 27)
status_note: In force; implemented by RTA resolutions
requirement_paraphrase: 'Vehicle' includes machines built to run on Roads; an AV may not travel on a Road unless RTA-licensed; a Permit is needed per Activity; licensing requires the RTA-prescribed technical inspection, conformity to UAE-approved specifications and UAE-licensed insurance; changes to the Autonomous Driving System or ODD need prior RTA approval; the Operator must immediately notify Competent Entities of any accident and provide data on request; the ADS must be capable of connecting to RTA-adopted systems; the Operator is liable for damage.
applies_to: AV operators and agents in Dubai (roads)

instrument: RTA Administrative Resolution No. (939) of 2025 (AV executive rules)
edition_or_version: Issued 10 Nov 2025; effective on Official Gazette publication (Art. 16)
status_note: English text is a translation; Arabic prevails
requirement_paraphrase: Covers light/heavy autonomous vehicles, buses, autonomous equipment and machinery, motorcycles. Art. 3 safety assessment: manufacturer-country compliance certificate, public-road test certificate, UAE conformity certificate, local operational test runs with data to RTA, design safety showing, RTA-approved speed/lane/zone system. Art. 4 emergency communication with Operator. Art. 14: operators notify malfunctions, store operational data securely, apply secure software updates.
